caveat: Partial correctness and model safety under the pinned 64-bit Go model, with package initialization and owned inputs as preconditions; compiler/runtime correctness, OOM and termination are excluded. Generated opaque type declarations remain and are reported by the theorem axiom sets. Complete all-input/all-owned-destination Header API composition is checked against independent HeaderFirstSpec/HeaderFullSpec, but requires Utf8ValidatorContract. The complete actual UTF-8 validator loop reduces that premise to Utf8WordWindowContract; the actual generic eight-byte helper remains unproved because the documented trusted slice-index repair is unapplied. Integer-key dispatch is checked for every input conditional on the same Utf8ValidatorContract, because even unknown text keys are validated before their values are skipped. Complete public BigInt decoding is now checked against independent integer success/rejection relations, with exact values, consumption, owned outputs/errors, input preservation and rollback; the pinned errors.Is comparability model is restricted here to concrete pointer targets. Public Cursor.Int64 and the complete typed signed-array helper are also checked for every byte input without helper premises; arrays preserve nil/empty distinctions and specify unsigned-overflow consumption, signed-fallback rollback and destination preservation on errors. Relevant initialization establishes actual immutable tables and error-category objects after modeled runtime CPU startup. Resource-key map, transaction-interface and class-interface witnesses are checked, but they are not payload decoder proofs; felt-key maps expose a separate array-equality modeling gap. All 15 manifested destinations have registered typed readers: Header, its five projections, BlockTransactionsIndexes, the receipt family, Transaction, transactionHashProjection, StateUpdate and ClassDefinition. BlockTransactionsIndexes now has conditional all-input/all-owned-destination contracts against independent IndexesFirstSpec/IndexesFullSpec, including initialization, nil/empty distinctions, both arrays, first-key-wins, exact suffixes and parser/trailing/guard errors; independent outcome uniqueness/separation is checked. NextWanted has a conditional all-input scan contract with initialized error categories and exact state/diagnostic ownership; projection record composition remains open. Projection, receipt, transaction, state-update and class implementations are translated and behavior-tested, but their complete decoder contracts remain open. Transaction and class decoding take explicit tag profiles; its connection to registry initialization is outside the proof boundary. Projection table initialization is checked for all seven tables; receipt, transaction, state and class payload-table initialization proofs remain open. The manifest and saved no-fallback corpus results are source-specific evidence, not formal fxamacker equivalence. Ignored CBOR text is intentionally not always validated, so successful decoding is not blanket RFC validity. The frozen performance gate passes for the recorded source hashes; no universal performance or whole-library correctness theorem is claimed.
